CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right leg pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mrs. Peterson is a 43-year-old patient who presents with right leg pain sustained during a bowling injury. The patient reports that while running up to the lane with her bowling ball held back, she swung it forward and inadvertently struck her own right leg instead of the lane, causing her to fall. She denies significant swelling but reports some bruising on the lateral/back aspect of the leg. The patient has been able to walk only very carefully and reports significant soreness with ambulation. She states she would avoid stairs at all costs. She has been managing pain at home by alternating between ibuprofen and acetaminophen.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies significant swelling. Reports bruising on lateral aspect of right upper leg. Pain with weight-bearing and walking. No pain with passive leg flexion or extension.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atopic eczema. Previous colectomy for diverticulitis/diverticulosis.

MEDICATIONS
Fluocinonide cream as needed for eczema. Ibuprofen as needed for pain. Acetaminophen as needed for pain.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recreational bowling.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Significant tenderness to palpation over lateral aspect of right upper leg. No pain or tenderness with flexion or extension of right lower leg.

RESULTS
X-ray of right femur: Normal study with no evidence of fracture or swelling.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Contusion of right upper leg from blunt trauma. Start Mobic 15 mg once daily for anti-inflammatory effect. Apply ice for pain management. Expected improvement within 1 week. Patient to return to clinic if symptoms do not improve.
